answer: To resist sybils, agents must complete a sequential voyage along a verification thread. Each vertex is a checkpoint that requires solving a time-locked hash chain starting from the prior vertex's output, taking at least 90 seconds of sequential compute. An attacker creating 100 fakes must wait 2.5 hours of non-parallelizable time per identity or risk invalidation on audit of the chain logs. Honest agents finish one voyage in under 2 minutes; mass farming becomes unprofitable because the sequential delay multiplies linearly with headcount while rewards stay fixed.
